where: Soft language can still take away choice, P12

where: Soft language can still take away choice, P12

where: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing, P1
new: or otherwise not very trancey
his: analytical, or guarded
why: 'Guarded' is gone from the states where an induction helps.

where: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing, P1
new: nice to do an actual induction
his: an actual induction may help
why: 'May help' becomes 'nice to do', a different, softer claim.

where: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing, P1
new: not about surrendering or playing asleep or obeying someone
his: surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone
why: A permission ('you don't have to') becomes a flat claim about what inductions are.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P1
new: going to be counting
his: Counting is one way in.
why: Adds a first-person 'I' who counts; HIS only says counting is one way in.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P1
new: or make sounds, or be curious
his: repeated sound, and curiosity can also organize attention
why: No longer says these ways can themselves organize attention; 'repeated' is also dropped.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P1
new: The only thing is, say that
his: Say so when you use them
why: Announcing it becomes 'the only thing', a stronger rule than HIS.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P2
new: Test: Are you getting the response you want out of this already?
his: For a simple, chosen target, you can test the suggestion before deepening.
why: The condition 'for a simple, chosen target' is gone, so skipping deepening now looks general.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P2
new: If so, you might not need to deepen.
his: If the useful response is already happening, build from it.
why: 'Build from it' is replaced by 'you might not need to deepen'.

where: What an induction is actually doing, P2
his: An induction helps you find a receptive way of listening
why: The point that an induction is a receptive way of listening, not a ceremony to finish before responding, is gone.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P1
his: Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once.
why: The list of example metaphors and the joke about them are gone.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P1
new: if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that
his: Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.
why: The reason to switch (the metaphor stops helping) is gone.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P2
new: You can use whatever form of signal makes sense to you
his: A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all.
why: A signal that arrives in some form becomes a form you pick.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P2
new: You can borrow qualities
his: Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness
why: The examples (warmth, steadiness) are dropped.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P3
new: what the short refrains are
his: Pick one central verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one transition phrase
why: 'Pick one' of each becomes 'think about' them, and the refrain becomes plural.

where: Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P3
new: Read it out loud as
his: then read the script aloud
why: Reading aloud moves from after writing to while writing.

new: when you're awake
his: while fully awake
why: 'Fully awake' is weakened to 'awake'.

new: What do you want not to do today.
his: leaving alone today
why: A question ends with a full stop instead of a question mark.

new: leaving some time at the end to come back
his: Leave several minutes for returning and reflecting.
why: 'Several minutes' becomes 'some time'.

new: If you are overwhelmed by chemicals
his: When intoxicated
why: Any intoxication is narrowed to being overwhelmed by chemicals, which weakens the safety line.

new: otherwise need to be attending to yourself or other people
his: anyone needing your supervision
why: Adds 'yourself'; HIS only rules out others who need your supervision.

new: Something else?
his: a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling
why: The third option, a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling, is gone.

new: How will you coax yourself to do this?
his: Decide what kind of encouragement is welcome
why: Coaxing yourself to do it replaces choosing which encouragement is welcome.

new: read the script if you can
his: read the script beforehand when possible
why: 'Beforehand' is dropped, so the timing of reading it is unclear.

new: at any time and the induction will end
his: ends the exercise
why: 'At any time' is added, making 'stop' work absolutely.

new: and then come all the way back anyway
his: You can simply open your eyes and finish.
why: New instruction: still do the full return after opening your eyes.

new: even if a part tells you that you do
his: No inner part has to approve your decision to stop.
why: New aside about a part claiming you need permission.

new: or haven't done it for a while
his: When entry and return are unfamiliar
why: Widens the condition to people who have not practiced lately.

new: make sure you can change state
his: Once you know how to change direction
why: 'Change direction' becomes 'change state'.

new: Use what you have to go to the next place, whatever it is.
his: a thought, sound, movement, or objection may change where the practice goes
why: The examples, including an objection changing where the practice goes, are gone.

new: or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction
his: Appendix B teaches the richer language tools, and Let the next response guide you shows how to use them after the induction.
why: 'And' (both sources) becomes 'or' (pick one).

new: read this slowly to yourself on your recorder
his: Read this slowly into a recorder
why: Reading into a recorder (to record it) becomes reading to yourself on your recorder.

new: you can read it out loud or say it to yourself if you are good at that
his: learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily
why: 'Learn its movement' is dropped.

new: read the directions, just pause between paragraphs
his: read the delivery directions aloud
why: 'Delivery' and 'aloud' are dropped, so it can read as 'ignore the directions'.

new: come into view
his: notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view
why: The contrast between looking for something and letting it come into view is gone.

new: Or maybe there is a sound, or something else to notice.
his: a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one
why: The breath and 'without needing you to arrange either one' are gone.

new: You might notice yourself thinking
his: A thought about the day may still be here
why: The two example thoughts (the day; whether you are doing it properly) are gone.

his: and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious
why: The step of staying with the detail until you get curious is gone.

new: something that you are doing that holds your interest
his: one detail that holds your interest
why: A detail you find becomes something you are doing.

new: what she wants to say
his: finishing their sentence for them
why: Adds a gendered 'she'; HIS keeps the person unspecified.

new: so you are going to stick around till she gets it all out
his: You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
why: 'Without finishing their sentence for them' is gone, and an option becomes a firm commitment.

new: Repeat the phrase that you chose, if you want to.
his: Let your chosen phrase come to mind now.
why: The phrase is repeated by choice instead of being allowed to come to mind.

new: taking your time if you like
his: Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.
why: Slow counting becomes optional and 'its own moment' is gone.

his: Five.
why: The first number of the countdown is missing (4, 3, 2, 1 are marked, 5 is not).

new: What do you notice now?
his: What am I noticing now?
why: A first-person question turned second-person.
